method.pairReports: Match artifact name, artifact-relative JSON path and RFC 6901 JSON pointer. Read dict/list values recursively; stop at full assessment results (setups, jobsAttempted, phaseTimings) or phase objects with outcomes.
method.deduplicate: When a row contains result and report.result, require exact deep equality, retain report.result once. Require summary.publicExamples to equal the corresponding fields of public-consumer-examples.json, omit that duplicate file. Keep separately executed scenarios, repeated runs and other hosts, even when their outcome lists are identical.
method.outcomeChecks: Require unique identities per phase/report; compare every retained outcome field except setups, evidence and executionMs. This includes IDs, local IDs, verdicts, countedAsKilled and pseudoTested where present. Load-failure rows also compare the status fields of their evidence (state, exit, cancelled, timedOut, error, outputTruncated, pipeError, cleanupError) as evidenceState. The ID-only Node load rows still cannot prove source-edit identity.
method.snapshots: Baseline and candidate retain scalar phase counters and timings, enabled operators, full perOperator rows and any phaseTimings, plus full report completeness, cancellation, signal, quality when present, and setup job states, exit codes, error fields, selection, counts, time limits and timings. Shared outcome lists are interned under outcomeSets; sharedOutcomesRef applies unchanged to both builds. addedOutcomesRef applies only to candidate; removedOutcomesRef only to baseline.
method.sourceChecks: Compare complete source results with no normalisation: 0.12.0 and 0.12.1 both emit coverageSuppressions. Retain SHA-256 of the source arrays encoded as UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, compact separators and literal Unicode, and every difference.
method.assessmentChanges: Compare each report except sources (compared in full above), outcomes (compared by identity above), diagnostics, keys ending Ms or named ms/timings/phaseTimings, and executionId. Runner reports, worker baselines and prepared baselines stay in the comparison; their temporary-directory prefixes are reduced to base file names and per-run capture IDs (capture-<pid>-<clock>-) in text are masked. Every difference outside those normalisations is retained and classified as jobCount, cancelledExitCode or unclassified; the normalised ones are only counted (normalisations.runnerReportTemporaryPathsAndCaptureIds).
method.fullReportJobArithmetic: Sum setup baseline, coverage and direct typecheck jobs (one when their job object has ms), plus each compilerStrictness.job (one), phase jobsAttempted, workerBaselineJobs and preparedBaselineJobs. setup attemptedJobs fields retain this derivation. Assert sum equals report jobsAttempted, in both builds.
method.hashes: Artifact digest is GitHub metadata. The four 0.12.1 latest-Node ZIPs were downloaded, checked against it and extracted with path checks. zipcheck.py then downloaded every compared artifact ZIP of both builds into memory, checked it against its GitHub digest and required each extracted JSON file used here to equal its ZIP member byte for byte. Every compared source JSON file has the SHA-256 of its raw bytes.
method.timings: Retain original floating-point milliseconds, including nulls and partial-report availability. Timings are single shared-runner samples; no performance claim.
method.reproduce: For each artifacts.files entry, verify raw JSON SHA-256, follow pointers, apply the deduplication and identity rules, then reconstruct baseline outcomes from shared+removed and candidate outcomes from shared+added references. Compare the two stored snapshots using the rules above.

normalisations.runnerReportTemporaryPathsAndCaptureIds: 639 per-run temporary path or capture-ID differences in 85 report results are compared by base file name or with capture IDs masked. The names and every other report field (counts, test IDs, states) remain compared.
normalisations.sources: None. Source arrays are compared in full and 0.12.0 and 0.12.1 already share the same coverageSuppressions format.
normalisations.perOperator: None. Both builds already emit eligibleSites and excludedSites.

equivalentMutants.basis: Discarding the numeric literal in equivalent() and dropping terminal bare returns in terminal() and values() do not change this fixture. The functions do not reflect on source. These closed examples do not estimate equivalence elsewhere.

Discarding the numeric literal in equivalent() and dropping terminal bare returns in terminal() and values() do not change this fixture. The functions do not reflect on source. These closed examples do not estimate equivalence elsewhere.

limits: No builds, dependency installation or new assessments were run. This compares the retained CI artifacts of the two direct heads, rather than rerunning fixtures locally.

The 130 Node load-failure reports (210 outcomes per build) retain outcome ID, verdict and evidence status but no source edit identity. Identity claims for them are limited to IDs and scenario positions.

Statement operator proof rows retain only the operator phase and totalJobsAttempted. Their per-mutant identities are not retained; the proof facts (semantics, fixture hashes, equivalent mutants) are compared separately and the proof source file is byte-identical at both heads.

Runner diagnostics, individual setup execution receipts, execution IDs, load-failure diagnostic text and temporary filesystem paths are excluded from outcome comparison; temporary-directory prefixes in runner reports are reduced to base file names and capture IDs in text are masked. Source arrays are compared in full.
Reports without an outer CLI envelope have no retained quality state. Missing partial-report metrics remain missing, not zero.

Scheduling-sensitive job counts (the source-error scenario) and Windows exit codes of cancelled child processes vary between runs of the same build. A single retained run of each cannot show that either build differs systematically; the censuses show the spread inside each build.
The linux-x64-debian-stage-evidence artifact of the Linux x64 runs, the build logs and archives in each package artifact are outside this comparison (it covers the 12 artifacts named in artifacts[]).
Timings are one sample per scenario on shared hosts. No speedup, rare-failure fix, notice audit, stage validation, installation check or publication approval is inferred.
